recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should be resource-specific or IG-specific if a particular resource lacks needed entered-in-error handling semantics; no additional core-wide lifecycle wording is indicated.
issue_request: FHIR-5175 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 MnM request to rationalize resources that can be nullified or marked entered-in-error versus resources where deletion or other handling is sufficient, and to add clear guidance rather than a universal nullifier element.
initial_application: No git commit directly naming FHIR-5175 was found. Jira comments say it was applied under another task; FHIR-5171 identifies SVN revision 4531, mirrored as git commit 07e5ff1f68a745c7d2a3c0a6acf98b8d26a92619, which created the lifecycle page and entered-in-error summary table.
additional_context: source/lifecycle.html is active through publish.ini and currently defines entered-in-error as accidental resource creation to be ignored, includes the entered-in-error table, and says erroneous-data handling is business-process-specific. source/status-codes.xml defines entered-in-error as invalid and often not removable for record integrity; conformance rules explain its modifier implications. FHIR-32165 and FHIR-I minutes later confirmed IG/resource-specific handling rather than generic core rules.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current specification already conveys the accepted issue-family decision and adding new generic delete-versus-flag prose would duplicate or broaden later accepted guidance.

related_jiras.note: Companion Published issue whose resolution and SVN revision 4531 created the lifecycle/entered-in-error tracking that FHIR-5175 explicitly referenced.
Later Published clarification refined the lifecycle page and confirmed that erroneous-data handling should not have generic core rules beyond IG/resource-specific guidance.
